title: Throughput/latency matrix for FP8 & INT8 variants with cache-coalescing and adversarial long-contexts
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Purpose: produce a dense throughput x latency matrix for FP8 and INT8 model variants across a realistic mix of request sizes, adversarial long-context sessions, and mixed-batch coalescing behavior. This spike quantifies how cache-coalescing (KV cache preloading + prefix joins) interacts with batching heuristics and memory/allocator behavior on multi-GPU NUMA nodes. Goal is to: 1) identify operating points where quantized variants regress tail latency or degrade accuracy beyond tolerances; 2) produce mitigations (batcher tuning, cache warmup, allocator flags) and clear acceptance criteria for shipping quant profiles in runtime-2.2.
acceptance_criteria: Complete matrix for FP8 & INT8: batch sizes [1,4,8,16], seq lengths [512,2048,8192], concurrency levels [4,16,64]
p50/p95/p99 token latency and throughput curves for each cell recorded and uploaded to benchmark dashboard
Identify at least two root causes for any >25% p99 regression vs FP32 baseline and propose mitigations
Calibration/accuracy: run eval harness on standard prompt set (1000 seeds) and show <1% answer-level accuracy drop vs FP32 for accepted profile
Runbook: short triage steps for observed memory fragmentation or NUMA stall scenarios
PR with runtime flags and batcher policy suggestions merged behind feature flag
run_steps: Provision perf nodes: r-infer-perf-rtx8000-nodes (2x per config, NUMA-aware) via infra/bench templates
Deploy runtime build with perf build tag runtime-2.2-ENG61234 to perf cluster
For each matrix cell: run bench_runner --model <variant> --batch N --seq L --concurrency C --kv-warmup 0/50/100 --allocator jemalloc/hoard --numa-mode interleave
Collect perf: prometheus push + flamegraphs + nvprof traces; export to s3 and link dashboard
Annotate and upload results to Confluence and link to this ticket
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting — scoped matrix, infra and node types confirmed. Decided on jemalloc vs default allocator comparison.
2026-02-27: Initial fp8/INT8 calibration runs completed on short-context (512). Observed 8-12% throughput improvement vs FP32 for FP8 with no accuracy drop in small prompts.
2026-03-03: Long-context (8192) dry runs revealed p99 tail spikes for INT8 at batch=8 when KV warmup=0; suspected allocator fragmentation and scheduler preemption as contributors.
2026-03-08: Reproduced tail on NUMA interleaved mode; enabling cache preloading (kv-warmup=100) reduced p99 by ~40% but reduced throughput ~6% for some configs.

2026-03-12: Draft mitigation options (batcher soft-deadline tweaks, kv-warmup defaults, jemalloc arenas tuning) assembled; performance regressions tracked in dashboard. Preparing PR for runtime flags behind feature flag.
open_questions: Is the small throughput loss from kv-warmup acceptable for Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs?
Should default runtime for FP8 profiles enable jemalloc arena tuning or leave as opt-in?
Do we need a per-model profile for cache preloading or a global heuristic based on recent seq length histogram?
notes_for_release: Documented recommended defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted in runtime-2.2 release notes
Include benchmark dashboard links and abbreviated runbook in release docs
triage_runbook: If p99 spikes: collect flamegraph + nvprof + allocator stats; check kv_cache_hit_rate and memory_frags_ratio
If NV linking shows kernel stalls: escalate to kernel-scheduling team and attach dmesg and perf.data
If accuracy drift >1%: re-run calibration with 3 seeds and fallback to next-safe quant profile (int8->fp8->fp32) via rollout policy
final_summary: Work will produce an actionable matrix and a small set of runtime defaults and batcher policy changes to unlock quantized profiles for long-context workloads without causing unacceptable tail latency or accuracy regressions. Deliverables: artifacts uploaded, PR merged behind feature flag, release notes, and an ops triage runbook.
